Subject: Acme MAP orientation — Private deployment owners & network/KMS alignment

Hi Sarah and team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the Private deployment evaluation. Per our pre-call, I’m starting a short mutual action plan (MAP) thread to align owners and timelines for networking, IAM/KMS, and deployment topology. Goal is a 6-week evaluation window with a production-readiness checklist at the end.

High-level asks from Acme we need owners for:
- Network / VPN / Transit connectivity (public IPs, CIDRs, expected throughput)
- IAM & KMS owner (BYOK vs Redwood-managed key, rotation policy)
- Deployment topology stakeholder (VPC/subnets, NAT, routing, peering)
- Security reviewer for SOC2 / audit evidence

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the internal owners (names + emails) for the bullets above by EOD Wed?
2) I’ve attached our MAP template and a sample network diagram. Please fill the owners column and attach any existing network diagrams.
3) We’ll propose a detailed evaluation plan (milestones and dates) after we have owners.

Attachments: redwood_map_template_v2.xlsx (MAP template), network-diagram-sample.png
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AexampleMAPfolder

Proposed timeline (subject to owner availability):
- Week 0: Owner alignment + baseline diagrams
- Week 1–2: Network & IAM connectivity setup (VPN/peering, KMS work)
- Week 3–4: Test workload run / smoke tests
- Week 5–6: Performance eval, security evidence collection, close decision

If there are scheduling constraints (change windows, freeze dates), call them out and we’ll adapt the plan.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi all — great, thanks Sarah for the owners. A few clarifications from the Redwood engineering side and a suggested technical plan.

Network / VPN options
- IPSec site-to-site is fine for initial eval. We can also support AWS Transit Gateway peering if you prefer (recommended if you later want multiple VPCs with shared services).
- For IPSec we’ll need either: a) a public IP and a reachable endpoint on Acme side, or b) a NAT + outbound connectivity that allows tunnel initiation from Redwood. Miguel, can you confirm which you prefer?
- Expected CIDR: please share the VPC CIDRs you intend to use (we prefer non-overlapping /24 to /20 ranges).

IAM & KMS
- We support BYOK via customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS CMK) or Redwood-managed keys. For FIPS/HSM requirements, we do have integrations with partner HSMs — Priya, if you have specific rotation/attestation requirements please share.
- If you plan BYOK: provide the KMS ARN and a user/service principal that can grant decrypt/encrypt rights to the Redwood service account. We’ll send the exact IAM policy template.

Deployment topology
- Typical test topology we propose (we'll share a diagram): 2 private subnets for inference nodes, 1 public subnet for NAT/bastion (if needed).
- IPs needed for health checks: 10.0.10.0/28 (sample) — we'll adjust to your plan.

Attachments and artifacts
- Attached: redwood-kms-options.pdf (KMS patterns and sample IAM policies), network-diagram-sample.png (example topology), redwood_map_template_v2.xlsx (filled sample tab).
- Drive folder with checklist and runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AexampleMAPfolder

Suggested short timeline (updated):
- Tue Oct 5: Confirm connectivity option + provide CIDRs and public IP plan
- Wed Oct 6–Fri Oct 15: VPN setup + KMS policy exchange (note change freeze Oct 11–15; we’ll do prep work but avoid infra changes during freeze)
- Mon Oct 18–29: Run smoke tests, collect logs, security evidence

Next actions for Acme: send CIDRs, public IP preference, KMS ARN (if BYOK), and a primary Slack/Teams channel for day-to-day coordination.

Cheers,
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Acme MAP orientation — Private deployment owners & network/KMS alignment

Adding a couple of technical points to help Miguel / Dan with network prep:
- If you go IPSec, please confirm the encryption params (AES-256, SHA256) and whether tunnel MTU will be default. Large MTU helps inference payloads; we can accommodate fragmentation but prefer 1500+ if possible.
- Health-check and KV cache endpoints: we recommend opening TCP 443 for outbound to Redwood IPs (we'll provide an allowlist).
- If you anticipate egress NAT for multiple teams, consider tagging a dedicated NAT gateway for the inference VPC so we can isolate traffic and SLOs.
- For KMS: Redwood needs kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey permissions scoped to the CMK ARN. We’ll provide a minimal policy template in the drive.

I’ve attached a short vpn-checklist.md and a snippet of our recommended security group rules.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference
